correctness.rationale: For algebraically closed k of prime characteristic p>=5, set y=t^(p+1), x=t^(p+2)u. The equation after dividing out t^((p+1)(p+2)) is u^(p+1)+1+lambda*t^(p^2-2p-5)*u^(p-1)=0. Its simple roots at t=0 lift. The orbit of x(t) under t->zeta*t has size p+1 by its leading exponent coprime to p+1; since the polynomial is monic of degree p+1 in x, this establishes irreducibility. In the Weierstrass basis 1,x,...,x^p over k[[y]], valuations are distinct modulo p+1, yielding semigroup <p+1,p+2> and delta p(p+1)/2. The coprime weighted initial Jacobian monomials x^p,y^(p+1) give mu=p(p+1). Writing M=x^(p-1)y^(p-1), the Jacobian relations give [f]=(5lambda/2)[M], and the maximal basis weight shows that (M) has basis M,yM. This gives the two Tjurina cases. For lambda nonzero the Frobenius induction keeps precisely the top monomial with exponent pair (p^e-1,p^e-1) at N=(p^e-1)/(p-1), killed by one more copy of f. At zero, f in (x^p,y^p) gives the upper bound p^(e-1)-1 on nu_e; at that degree the balanced binomial term is nonzero by Lucas and fits in the exponent box. Frobenius powers of the maximal ideal are preserved by local automorphisms, and units preserve ideal membership, so the distinct thresholds separate the p=5 strata. These exact arguments, not the finite script, cover all parameters.
residual_risks: The parenthetical root-order wording at RESULT.md line 28 is imprecise: the simple equation in u at t=0 has degree p+1, not p+2. The stated substitution and Hensel premise yield the valuations and semigroup as verified above.
